functions.name: monkilled
functions.sourceReview: Compared mon.c:3377-3416. C prints only when fltxt is non-null and either worm_known succeeds for a worm or cansee succeeds for other monsters; otherwise it defers the sad feeling. JS now uses the same conditional, preserving the empty-string versus null distinction and the existing mondied/mondead order. This is a narrow caller-parity correction, not whole-function certification or public input parity.

entryPointReview: The fixed test seed initializes a normal long worm and ordinary planning state. A first real runSimpleMonsterAction movement creates the allocated segment and future growtime; the selected second movement reaches a fresh arrow trap, whose real thitm call passes empty-string fltxt to monkilled. The fixture enters that selected route at HP 1 with source-derived max HP and future growtime; it does not claim a public setup history or a separate prior-attack recording. The same focused command failed on the original source at the real monkilled refusal, then passed after the correction. Visibility controls cover visible tail with unseen head and all segments unseen. Runtime remains pending; there is no C recording, admitted synthetic range, public input recipe, or public parity claim.
